accepted.question: Explain how malware propagates and infects systems by describing the specific techniques used by boot sector viruses, executable file appenders, and network worms.

marking_points.point: Boot sector viruses spread by infecting the boot sector of distributed software diskettes or system drives.
marking_points.quote: Included in a boot sector of distributed software diskettes

marking_points.point: Executable COM viruses propagate by appending a virus body to a program and replacing the entry point with a jump to that body.
marking_points.quote: Append a virus body to a program Save an entry point to a program in a virus body Replace a program entry point with a jump to a virus body

marking_points.point: After execution, the virus code restores the original entry point and jumps to it to allow the host program to run normally.
marking_points.quote: Virus code restores the original entry point and jumps to it after its own execution

marking_points.point: Executable EXE viruses propagate by overwriting the program header to switch the entry point to the virus code.
marking_points.quote: Over write a program header to switch the entry point to a virus

marking_points.point: Network worms like the Morris worm propagated across networks such as Arpanet using remote execution features.
marking_points.quote: Used a debugging feature of sendmail (remote execution) Propagated in the Arpanet

marking_points.point: Worms can penetrate a significant number of computers rapidly, affecting availability and control of systems.
marking_points.quote: Penetrated ca.6,000 computers (10% of Arpanet)

accepted.question: State six characteristics of the Chinese Wall security model, covering its origin, classification, policy rules, and dynamic nature.

marking_points.point: The model was proposed by Brewer and Nash in 1989 to address conflicts of interest.
marking_points.quote: Brewer and Nash (1989) proposed a policy called the Chinese Wall Policy that addresses such conflicts of interest.

marking_points.point: It is strictly classified as an access control confidentiality policy rather than an integrity policy.
marking_points.quote: Strictly speaking, this is not an integrity policy, but an access control confidentiality policy.

marking_points.point: The simple security rule allows access if the object is within the same company datasets as previously accessed objects.
marking_points.quote: is in the same company datasets as the objects already accessed by s, that is, "within the Wall," or

marking_points.point: Alternatively, the simple security rule permits access if the object belongs to a different conflict of interest class.
marking_points.quote: belongs to an entirely different conflict of interest class.

marking_points.point: Write access requires that no object from a different company dataset containing unsanitized information has been read.
marking_points.quote: no object can be read which is: in a different company dataset than the one for which write access is requested, and contains unsanitized information.

marking_points.point: Access rights are dynamic because they depend on the history of past accesses by the subject.
marking_points.quote: Notice that permissions change dynamically. The access rights that any subject enjoys depends on the history of past accesses

questions.question: Explain how malware propagates and infects systems by describing the specific techniques used by boot sector viruses, executable file appenders, and network worms.

marking_points.point: Boot sector viruses spread by infecting the boot sector of distributed software diskettes or system drives.
marking_points.quote: Included in a boot sector of distributed software diskettes

marking_points.point: Executable COM viruses propagate by appending a virus body to a program and replacing the entry point with a jump to that body.
marking_points.quote:
Append a virus body to a program
Save an entry point to a program in a virus body
Replace a program entry point                                   with a jump to a virus body

marking_points.point: After execution, the virus code restores the original entry point and jumps to it to allow the host program to run normally.
marking_points.quote: Virus code restores the original                                 entry point and jumps to it after                                     its own execution

marking_points.point: Executable EXE viruses propagate by overwriting the program header to switch the entry point to the virus code.
marking_points.quote: Over write a program header to switch the entry point to a virus

marking_points.point: Network worms like the Morris worm propagated across networks such as Arpanet using remote execution features.
marking_points.quote:
Used a debugging feature of sendmail (remote execution)
Propagated in the Arpanet

marking_points.point: Worms can penetrate a significant number of computers rapidly, affecting availability and control of systems.
marking_points.quote: Penetrated ca.6,000 computers (10% of Arpanet)

snooping, sniffing, wiretapping

Modification

questions.question: Explain the mechanism and impact of the Samy worm as a case study of malware propagation via Cross-Site Scripting (XSS).

marking_points.point: The attack exploits web applications that return user input without filtering, allowing arbitrary JavaScript execution.
marking_points.quote: Any web application that returns user input without ﬁltering is a potential XSS vulnerability!

marking_points.point: The malware injects JavaScript into a user profile using document.body.innerHTML to modify the page content.
marking_points.quote: Inject Javascript into a user proﬁle using document.body.innerHTML

marking_points.point: It retrieves the list of the victim's friends by performing a GET request on their profile.
marking_points.quote: Get the list of user’s heros by using a GET on a user proﬁle

marking_points.point: The worm adds itself to the friend list by performing an XML-HTTP request to the addFriends page.
marking_points.quote: Add Samy as a ﬁeld by performing XML-HTTP on the addFriends page

marking_points.point: Propagation occurs automatically when any user visits an infected profile, infecting their own profile and friends list.
marking_points.quote: Any user who visits an infected user’s page will gets proﬁle infected with Javascript and his friends list infected with Samy

marking_points.point: The scale of the infection was significant, eventually compromising approximately one million MySpace profiles.
marking_points.quote: Eventually about 1,000,000 MySpace proﬁles were infected.

marking_points.quote: Strictly speaking, this is not an integrity policy, but an access control confidentiality policy.

no object can be read which is:
